title: Hymn and Cellar
premise: Orsen Kavanagh, an urban explorer who has spent twelve years rationalizing the sounds beneath his childhood town, returns home to find his imaginary friend Wren waiting on the porch, unchanged since he was nine. The tunnels he maps aren't on any survey because they belong to something that counts its residents — and when the count reaches a full number, it takes them. As Orsen's estranged family is drawn back to the house one by one, he must get them out ahead of the final tally, before the last resident, his dying grandmother, signs over the property and seals them all inside. In the end Orsen trades himself into the count to buy their escape, and Wren — who was never imaginary at all — breaks the ledger instead, freeing both of them into a dawn that no longer keeps records.
about_author: M. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former municipal surveyor who spent a decade documenting infrastructure that officially did not exist. They write horror about the gap between what maps say and what places remember.

chapters.title: The Porch Light
chapters.summary: Orsen Kavanagh returns to Hollow Creek to photograph condemned houses, POV his. On his grandmother's porch sits Wren, the imaginary friend he invented at nine, unchanged. The emotional beat is vertigo: twelve years of rational explanations collapse in a single greeting.

chapters.title: Survey Says Nothing
chapters.summary: Orsen cross-references his tunnel photos against county surveys; the passages simply aren't there. POV alternates to his sister Delia, arriving uninvited. Beat: creeping doubt as two skeptics find evidence neither can dismiss.

chapters.title: Wren Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Wren speaks only in things nine-year-old Orsen said, including promises Orsen forgot making. POV Orsen. He learns the tunnels 'count' residents, and the house is one signature from being sold. Beat: guilt resurfacing like water in a cellar.

chapters.title: Delia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Delia, a forensic accountant, finds the deed history: every owner died or vanished on anniversaries spaced exactly eleven years apart. POV hers. Beat: her need for order becomes the first weapon against the pattern.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Papers
chapters.summary: POV grandmother Edele, lucid for the first time in months. She knows about the count and has been stalling the sale deliberately, keeping herself the last resident so the number stays incomplete. Beat: fierce, exhausted love disguised as stubbornness.

chapters.title: Down Where the Air Moves
chapters.summary: Orsen explores the unmapped tunnel with Wren guiding him. He hears counting — patient, enormous, wrong. POV his. Beat: terror mixed with the awful comfort of being known completely by something inhuman.

chapters.title: Family Reunion, Reluctant
chapters.summary: Brother Tomas arrives with his kids for Edele's supposed last weeks. POV Tomas. The children hear the counting too, and one of them starts answering it. Beat: parental dread — duty to protect versus disbelief.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Noises
chapters.summary: Orsen finally tells Delia everything: the noises he explained away at sixteen, the night he left, why he never came back. POV his. Beat: confession as relief, and the first honest alliance between siblings.

chapters.title: What the Count Wants
chapters.summary: Wren explains the rules: the thing below needs a complete household to close its ledger, and signatures count as consent. POV Wren — strange, childlike, older than the town. Beat: tenderness and menace braided together.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: A developer's agent pressures Edele to sign; the papers feel less like commerce than bait. POV Delia investigating the developer, whose company has existed under different names since 1911. Beat: justice outside the law begins here.

chapters.title: The Kids' Game
chapters.summary: Tomas's daughter plays a hopping game that mirrors the tunnel layout exactly. POV Tomas watching, horrified. Beat: the horror moves upstairs; nowhere in the house is neutral ground anymore.

chapters.title: Cellar Door, Open
chapters.summary: Someone — something — opens the sealed cellar door from below. Edele stands at the top all night holding a hymnal, singing until dawn. POV Edele. Beat: faith as fortification, and its limits.

chapters.title: Running the Numbers
chapters.summary: Delia calculates: the count needs seven. The family plus Wren makes eight — one too many, unless someone leaves. POV hers. Beat: cold arithmetic colliding with found-family loyalty.

chapters.title: Tomas Breaks
chapters.summary: Tomas tries to take the kids and flee at 3 a.m.; the road loops back to the porch every time. POV his. Beat: the law of the outside world doesn't apply here — you can't outrun a census.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren offers to be counted in Orsen's place, revealing it once belonged to the tunnels before choosing a lonely boy above. POV Orsen refusing. Beat: love against duty — Orsen won't let Wren pay his debt.

chapters.title: The Signing
chapters.summary: Edele, weakening fast, nearly signs to end it on her own terms. Orsen intercepts the pen mid-stroke. POV alternating between them. Beat: the family's oldest wound — everyone trying to be sacrificed alone.

chapters.title: All Hands
chapters.summary: The family, for the first time united, plans together: forge the sale's failure, break the deed chain, starve the count of consent. POV Delia leading. Beat: found family forged in crisis, competence as hope.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Orsen goes down to confront the counter directly, Wren at his side, while the family holds the paperwork line above. POV his. Beat: rising dread as the tunnel fills with voices of every prior resident.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: Climax part one: the entity offers Orsen a choice — sign as last resident and free everyone, or watch it take them anyway when Edele dies naturally within days. POV his. Beat: duty wearing love's face.

chapters.title: Hymn in the Dark
chapters.summary: Climax part two: Edele's hymn drifts down through the floorboards; Wren remembers being sung to before the tunnels existed. Wren turns on the ledger itself. POV Wren. Beat: the counted becoming the counter-breaker.

chapters.title: Broken Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wren tears its own name from the count, leaving the ledger permanently incomplete; the tunnels exhale and go silent forever. Orsen carries Wren's fading form up into daylight. POV Orsen. Beat: grief and triumph inseparable.

chapters.title: No Records Kept
chapters.summary: Resolution: Edele dies peacefully unsigned, the house passes to the family jointly, and the surveyors finally map the tunnels — empty. Orsen stays, teaching his niece to explore safely. On the porch some evenings, a second porch light burns. Beat: quiet, earned peace with one open door.
